newsitem.title: SPAIN: Copper exports from Russia to remain high.
newsitem.headline: Copper exports from Russia to remain high.

text.p: There is likely to be a high level of copper exports from the former Soviet Union (FSU) for the next couple of years, until domestic consumption recovers, James May, analyst at Metal Bulletin Research (MBR) said.

"We see exports continuing to climb over the next two years to over 750,000 tonnes before starting to fall in 1998 as (local) consumption finally turns around," May said at Metal Bulletin's 10th International Copper Conference.

Exports from the FSU in 1996 were 75 percent of its production, due to the sharp contraction in domestic consumption in recent years. Whether exports rise or fall depends on changes in domestic consumption.
May said that the steep decline in apparent consumption may be slightly exaggerated, due to the depletion of stocks built up in the late 1980s, which were then exported.
However, there is little immediate light on the consumption horizon in the FSU at present.
"Although there are some signs for positive growth in end-u se sectors, this in most cases reflects a slowing of decline as opposed to a wholesale turnaround," May said.
Economic reforms in the region have up until recently been fairly cosmetic, so no recovery in consumption is expected for at least a further year.
The fall in exports, when it does eventually happen, should not have a major impact on the western market.
"We do not believe that this fall (in exports) will be sufficient to have a significant impact on the large surplus of metal being forecast over the next five years," May added.
